core_meaning.short_meaning: Pleasing satisfaction, noble threshold; early companion Utbah ibn Ghazwan.
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Utbah (عُتْبَة) is a historic Arabic masculine name meaning 'satisfaction, contentment, and pleasing graciousness' or 'the threshold of honor'. In Islamic history, it is the distinguished name of Utbah ibn Ghazwan, the seventh convert to Islam, veteran of Badr, and the pious ascetic founder and governor of Basra.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Derived from ʿataba/ʿutbā, conveying the removal of displeasure, attainment of divine favor, and a threshold of dignity.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The root ʿ-t-b signifies pleasing someone, seeking reconciliation, or a step/threshold. Utbah ibn Ghazwan al-Mazini was a confederate of Banu Nawfal who accepted Islam in its earliest days. He led the campaign into southern Iraq, founded the strategic city of Basra, and delivered a famous sermon on humility, worldly renunciation, and fear of God before passing away in 17 AH.

arabic.name: عُتْبَة

arabic.long_meaning: المعنى اللغوي لـعُتْبَة في هذا السجل هو «الرِّضا والعَتْب المستحب، والعَتَبَة مَدْرَجة الباب؛ الصحابي الجليل عُتْبَة بن غَزْوان سابع من أسلم وباني البصرة رضي الله عنه»؛ وهذه صياغة أولية تحتاج إلى مراجعة لغوية.
